CSTEP Training · for Finance

Reimburse, pay vendors and export to Tally

Verified claims and settled tours land with the Finance user mapped to the traveller. Reimburse them one at a time or many at once from the working sheet, pay the vendors behind every arranged trip the same way, and hand the paid lines to Tally as journal vouchers.

Part 1 of 5

Your Finance queue

Everything waiting for you to pay.

  1. 1Your dashboard
  2. 2Travel Claims → Approvals → Finance
QueueStep 1 of 2 · Dashboard

In your queues — action required

As the Finance user, your dashboard counts what is in your queues — every case waiting for reimbursement across your travellers.

You see a case because its traveller is mapped to you as their Finance user.

QueueStep 2 of 2 · Finance tab

Cases waiting for reimbursement

Travel Claims → Approvals opens Your Queues on the Finance tab: verified claims and settled tours, each Sent to reimbursement with its reference (TIN, LTC…, EXP…), project, period and traveller.

Bulk reimbursement sits on top. Export CSV and Export Travel Register are on the right.

Travel Claims → ApprovalsFinance
Part 2 of 5

Reimburse one case

Open a case, pay it, and close it.

  1. 1Finance — reimbursement
  2. 2Mark reimbursed, then confirm
  3. 3Closed
  4. 4Send back instead
One caseStep 1 of 4 · Open the case

Finance — reimbursement

Open a case from the queue. At the bottom, Finance — reimbursement shows the amount to reimburse — for this tour ₹3,040, the per diem plus what the traveller paid themselves, as settled by the Office.

Above it you can still see what was arranged and each vendor line's payment status.

One caseStep 2 of 4 · Mark reimbursed

Payment reference, then confirm the amount

Enter the payment reference (UTR / voucher no.) — optional but recommended — and click Mark reimbursed.

It asks you to confirm the exact amount: Confirm ₹3,040 reimbursed, or Cancel.

Payment referenceMark reimbursedConfirm ₹…
One caseStep 3 of 4 · Closed

Reimbursed — the case is closed

The status is REIMBURSED. The audit trail records FINANCE_SETTLE: the amount reimbursed to the traveller, the reference and the claim — under the Office's SETTLE entry.

The case leaves your queue.

One caseStep 4 of 4 · Send back

Something wrong? Send it back

If the amount doesn't look right, Send back to CSTEP Admin (a claim) or Send back to Official (a tour) with your reason — nothing is paid.

The Admin re-checks the lines and verifies again; it comes back to you. (Here we stop before Confirm send back.)

Part 3 of 5

Bulk reimbursement

Close many cases at once from the exported working sheet.

  1. 1Export the queue
  2. 2Fill Paid On and Payment Ref
  3. 3Import — preview first
  4. 4Commit
  5. 5What is left
BulkStep 1 of 5 · The working sheet

Bulk reimbursement

Export Excel downloads your queue as the working sheet — Reference, Traveller, Type, Net Amount, Advance, Status, and two empty columns: Paid On and Payment Ref.

Pay the cases in your bank, then fill those two columns on the rows you paid.

BulkStep 2 of 5 · Import

Import reimbursements

Import reimbursements: work from the Export (it carries your real queue, matched on Reference); the template is headers only.

Choose the filled sheet and click Preview import. Rows without a Paid On date are left alone, so you can import the whole sheet back.

Export queue (working sheet)Choose FilePreview import
BulkStep 3 of 5 · Preview

Preview — nothing is paid yet

The preview says exactly what will happen: Will close 3 cases · ₹7,212 paid out — each row Reimbursed · ₹amount, or Not marked (no Paid On date).

Each case is paid at its computed net amount — amounts typed in the sheet are ignored.

BulkStep 4 of 5 · Commit

Close the cases

Close 3 cases commits it: Closed 3 cases · ₹7,212 paid out, with a batch number for your records.

Every case closed this way records its Paid On date and reference, like a single reimbursement.

BulkStep 5 of 5 · After

What is left in the queue

The queue drops to the two cases you didn't mark — they wait for your next run.

Pay vendors

Every arranged line, with who it is owed to and whether it is paid.

  1. 1Vendor payables
  2. 2Mark paid on one line
  3. 3Import payments from the sheet
  4. 4Paid, with date and reference
VendorsStep 1 of 4 · Payables

Vendor payments — what is still to pay

The Vendor payments tab lists every arranged line for your travellers: vendor and code, the request reference, traveller, service, amount, status and paid on / ref.

It opens on Unpaid; filter by status, vendor or travel dates. The count shows lines and the total still unpaid.

Vendor paymentsStatus · vendor · dates
VendorsStep 2 of 4 · One line

Mark paid on the request

Click a reference to open the request. In What was arranged, Mark paid on the line: the UTR / cheque no., the vendor's invoice no. and the payment date, then Save payment.

The date cannot be in the future.

VendorsStep 2 of 4 · One line

Payment done

The line shows Payment done with its UTR, date and invoice number — Mark unpaid reverses it.

The hotel on the same trip is still Payment pending.

VendorsStep 3 of 4 · Bulk

Import vendor payments

For many lines at once: Export Excel (the payables working sheet), fill Paid On and Payment Ref on the lines you paid, then Import payments.

Choose the filled sheet and Preview import.

VendorsStep 3 of 4 · Bulk

Preview — line by line

Will mark 2 lines paid: each row shows its outcome — Paid, Already paid (left as it is) or Not marked paid (no Paid On date).

Then Mark 2 lines paid.

VendorsStep 3 of 4 · Bulk

Marked paid

Marked 2 lines paid, with a batch number. Nothing else in the sheet changed.

VendorsStep 4 of 4 · Paid

Every line, paid or not

With All statuses, every line shows Paid or Unpaid; a paid one carries its date and UTR, and whether it was Imported or marked by hand (Manual).

One hotel line is still unpaid — it stays on your list.

Part 5 of 5

Export to Tally

Paid vendor lines as the Tally journal upload — and the Travel Register.

  1. 1Tally settings (CSTEP Admin, once)
  2. 2Export to Tally for a period
  3. 3The Travel Register
TallyStep 1 of 3 · Settings

Tally settings — set once by the CSTEP Admin

The CSTEP Admin sets what the export writes: the company name as in Tally, the voucher type (Journal), a default expense ledger, and an expense ledger per vendor type (Airline → Air Travel Expenses, Hotel → Boarding & Lodging…).

The vendor's own ledger — its name — is always the credit side. The next voucher number comes from Numbering.

TallyStep 2 of 3 · Export

Export to Tally for the period

Vendor payments → Export to Tally: choose Paid from and Paid to. Every vendor line marked paid in that period is exported.

One journal voucher per paid line: Dr the expense ledger for the vendor's type, Cr the vendor.

Export to TallyPaid from · Paid toDownload for Tally
TallyStep 2 of 3 · Export

Downloaded — the Tally upload

Download for Tally saves the upload sheet (here cstep-tally-2026-10-01-to-2026-10-18.xlsx) to import into Tally.

A line keeps its voucher number for good, so exporting the same period again gives the same vouchers.

TallyStep 3 of 3 · Travel Register

Export Travel Register

Export Travel Register downloads an Excel register — one row per expense line, filed by departure date — for a week, month, quarter, financial year or a custom range.

Include drafts adds trips not yet submitted for approval.
